decisions.question: The three nidana.model contracts' Delivery paragraphs say a consumer's edge waits on nidana.model.3 or nidana.model.5 and name no `hard` edge, while nidana.integration's `hard` edges wait on each contract's last producing phase (nidana.integration D2). Does a Delivery paragraph need a change for this consumer?

options.label: add the hard-edge clause
options.consequence: one sentence per contract, 'A `hard` edge waits instead on nidana.model.{8,11,14}, the last producing phase (nidana.integration)', as the six other contracts already say; hsdd-config then carries the right wait into every nidana.integration phase context

options.label: leave the paragraphs unchanged
options.consequence: no edit, but the generic 'a consumer's edge ... waits on nidana.model.3/5' read literally gives nidana.integration.1 and .2 a wait their plan does not take, and nidana.integration D2's claim that each consumed contract's Delivery names its wait stays false for three contracts

decisions.why: Conventions (Contracts) say the reconcile that applies confirms writes the Delivery paragraph, including the phase a consumer's edge waits on. Written at S29, when nidana.integration was a node placeholder, these three paragraphs covered only `contract` and `shared-model` edges, so their generic sentence names a wrong phase for nidana.integration's `hard` edges (root edge table: every other child to nidana.integration is `hard`; root D10). The added sentence matches the plan's waits (nidana.integration.1 on nidana.model.8, .2 on nidana.model.11 and nidana.model.14) and the wording bus-api@v1, navigation-api@v1, flutter-binding@v1, topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 already use. No interface, guarantee or version changes, so no Versioning line, as earlier reconciles' Delivery writes carried none.

decisions.question: navigation-api@v1's Delivery says a `hard` edge waits on nidana.navigation.6 (nidana.integration), but the confirm makes nidana.integration.1 a consumer that declares `AppRoutes` against the declarations and waits on nidana.navigation.1. Is that wrong for this consumer?

options.label: name nidana.integration.1's wait on nidana.navigation.1
options.consequence: the paragraph says nidana.navigation.6 for nidana.integration from .2 on and adds that nidana.integration.1, compiling only, waits on nidana.navigation.1, as bus-api@v1's Delivery names nidana.flutter.1's compile-only wait on nidana.runtime.1

options.label: keep the node-level hard-edge wording
options.consequence: no edit, but hsdd-config would carry 'waits on nidana.navigation.6' into nidana.integration.1's context, contradicting its plan's dependency list and its confirm entry's rationale

decisions.why: The confirm entry's rationale and nidana.integration D2 rule 1 put nidana.integration.1 on nidana.navigation.1: it compiles `AppRoutes` against `NavRoute` and runs none of the contract's behavior; from nidana.navigation.1 on the const constructors assign their fields (the same paragraph). The old wording named a wrong phase for one of this consumer's phases, which is the case the step allows a correction for. Every other contract's Delivery names nidana.integration's waits correctly (bus-api@v1, bus-testing@v1: nidana.runtime.14, first consumer .3; flutter-binding@v1: nidana.flutter.7, first consumer .5; topic-codegen@v1: nidana.tooling.codegen.11; nidana-checks@v1: nidana.tooling.lint.4 for the plugin and nidana.tooling.codegen.11 for the scan, both before .1).

decisions.question: ADR-001 item 12 makes a fixtures directory the executable validation artifact only when it meets item 3 and its kind's items, checked by the structure set once the replay tool exists and by hsdd-reconcile by reading until then. On what check does each of the nine contracts flip to `stable`?

options.label: path existence plus the prototype structure check
options.consequence: every Validation path exists, every binding is listed, and the file-invocations prototype of item 3's coverage and item 9's layout reports 0 problems over the nine contracts; all nine flip

options.label: path existence alone
options.consequence: what hsdd-reconcile step 7 states literally; skips item 12's reading of coverage

options.label: hold every contract at draft until the replay tool runs
options.consequence: nothing flips; the final gate fails on nine contracts and every consumer phase context warns draft, although the rule says reading suffices until the tool exists

decisions.chosen: path existence plus the prototype structure check
decisions.why: It satisfies step 7 and does item 12's reading mechanically instead of by eye: 226 guarantees across nine contracts, each covered by a reject header, a behavior case name, a schema or file covers clause, an invocation row or a not-executable line; layouts and data directories as item 9 states; ten bindings listed. Reject codes and suites remain unverified against the real packages until the first replay (ADR-001 Consequences), which stable does not claim: stable is interface-frozen, not producer-shipped.

decisions.question: Notes 1 (the member and the shared root workspace list and lockfile) and 2 (the unrestricted replay first at nidana.integration.6, again at .7 and .8): do they change a convention?

options.label: drop both
options.consequence: conventions unchanged for them; the facts stay in nidana.integration D3, D4 and its phase sections

options.label: apply both
options.consequence: Shared workspace files would name nidana.integration.1 and Phase design would carry one node's replay schedule, plan data the conventions do not hold for any other node

decisions.why: Conventions (Shared workspace files) already name nidana.integration among the nodes whose one member-creating phase edits the workspace list and lockfile, without naming any node's phase; ADR-001 item 10 already places the tree's one unrestricted replay in nidana.integration's gate. Which phases run it is the plan's data (hsdd-reconcile step 10: drop notes that duplicate derived data).

decisions.question: Note 3: the root `fvm dart analyze` reads `build/` directories and no `.dart_tool/`. Does it change a convention?

options.label: apply as a Phase design rule for every gate
options.consequence: one bullet: a gate's Dart output that is not a committed source goes under `.dart_tool/` or a temporary directory, never `build/`; every node's planner and phase context sees it

options.label: leave it in nidana.integration D3
options.consequence: no conventions edit; a later phase of another node that writes generated Dart under `build/` would break every node's root analyze with no rule to cite

decisions.chosen: apply as a Phase design rule for every gate
decisions.why: The root analyze runs in every gate of every node, so one node's stray output under `build/` fails the others' gates: a cross-node rule, the kind the conventions hold. Experiment C2 widened S41's I6 to a member's `.dart_tool/`, where topic-codegen@v1's `catalog` writes its entry point: neither the root's nor a member's `.dart_tool/` is read, both `build/` directories are. The rule is worded for output that is not a committed source, since nidana.integration.1 and .8 run build_runner, which writes the committed `lib/topics.g.dart`. No current plan writes Dart under `build/`.

decisions.question: Note 4: a Flutter member's test finds the pinned `dart` at `$FLUTTER_ROOT/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dart` and can drive the toolchain from it. Does it change a convention?

options.label: apply beside the ancestor-search rule
options.consequence: two sentences in the existing bullet on member tests: a Flutter member's test that runs the toolchain spawns the pinned `dart` from `FLUTTER_ROOT`, never a `dart` from `PATH`, because `Platform.resolvedExecutable` is the `flutter_tester` there

options.label: leave it in nidana.integration D6 and D9
options.consequence: no conventions edit; the owner's 'always fvm dart, never a bare dart' rule has no stated form for processes a test spawns

decisions.why: It is the toolchain convention applied to processes a test spawns, and it sits beside the conventions' existing Flutter-test fact (`Isolate.resolvePackageUri` throws, so ancestor search). Today only nidana.integration's tests spawn the toolchain, so the case is close; the signal that would have changed my mind is certainty that no other Flutter member's test ever spawns a tool, which a retro phase or a later version of nidana.flutter can break. The temporary-package analysis technique (I3, I4) stays node-local in D6.

decisions.question: Note 5: build_runner 2.16.1 has removed `--delete-conflicting-outputs` and silently rewrites a stale committed output. Does it change a convention?

options.label: drop as node-local
options.consequence: the fact stays in nidana.integration D7, which orders its gates accordingly

options.label: apply to conventions
options.consequence: a rule for gates that check committed generated files, of which nidana.integration's are the only ones

options.label: route to ADR-002 through hsdd-adr
options.consequence: ADR-002 Consequences, which already governs where build_runner runs, would record the flag's removal; an ADR step for a fact no artifact contradicts

decisions.why: ADR-002 Consequences confines build_runner to `packages/nidana_integration`, the one member that applies the builders and the only one committing generated output, and D7 already holds the fact and the ordering. No artifact passes the removed flag (grep of hsdd/), so nothing is stale. Listed below as an optional ADR-002 touch.

decisions.question: nidana-checks@v1 In CI says nidana.integration's gate 'runs the same steps' as an app's CI (build_runner, then analyze, catalog and scan into `build/`), while nidana.integration.8 runs build_runner after its tests (D7) and writes every output under `.dart_tool/nidana_integration/` (D3). Edit the sentence in this reconcile?

options.label: leave it and report
options.consequence: the contract body changes only through entries; a later hsdd-contract touch or consistency pass rewords the informative sentence

options.label: reword it now
options.consequence: accurate at once, but a contract body edit no entry asked for and outside the Delivery paragraph this step may correct

decisions.why: The sentence is informative, states no guarantee, and is not contradicted in substance: the same commands run over the same package, with a different output directory and build_runner placed later for D7's staleness check. Body edits belong to amend entries or hsdd-contract. Not a collision under hsdd-reconcile step 3: no second node claims anything and no amend is involved.
